prompt: Repair this C99 event-stream decoder without changing its public API or CLI output. A wire record consists of four header bytes: magic 0xD3, kind (1=text, 2=binary, 3=ping), and a big-endian unsigned 16-bit payload length, followed by exactly that many payload bytes. Ping must have length zero. Text must contain no NUL bytes; binary permits every byte. Empty text and binary are valid. decoder_create(max_payload, callback, user) requires a non-NULL callback and max_payload <=65535 (zero is valid); invalid arguments or allocation failure return NULL. A decoder accepts arbitrary feed fragmentation, including one-byte feeds, headers/payloads split anywhere, and many records per call. It must deliver each complete valid record exactly once in order, never deliver a partial or invalid record, and stop at the first invalid record while retaining callbacks for valid preceding records. Header validation occurs as soon as all four header bytes are available, rejecting bad magic, unknown kind, oversize length, or nonempty ping without waiting for the payload. Text NUL rejection occurs when its complete payload is available. decoder_feed returns 0 on success and -1 on malformed input, invalid NULL data with nonzero size, or allocation failure; errors are sticky, so every later feed (even size zero) and finish returns -1 until reset. NULL data with size zero is otherwise a successful no-op. decoder_finish returns 0 at a record boundary (including an empty stream), or -1 and enters the sticky error state if any header or payload is incomplete; a successful finish does not seal the decoder, so feeding more records remains valid. decoder_reset discards partial input and error state without callbacks, preserving the limit, callback, and user pointer. decoder_destroy also discards partial input and accepts NULL. Other decoder arguments must be valid handles. Callback ownership: each callback receives its own heap-allocated packet and owns it until packet_free; the decoder must not free or reuse delivered packets. packet_free accepts NULL. The packet data is independent of feed buffers and remains valid after further feeds, reset, and decoder destruction. Its length excludes an extra trailing NUL byte, which must exist at data[length] even for empty or binary packets. Callbacks may retain or free packets immediately, but must not call feed, finish, reset, or destroy on the same decoder from inside a callback. All resource paths must be leak-free and memory-safe. The event_dump CLI reads raw records from stdin and prints kind:length:lowercase-hex-payload plus newline per delivered event; it returns 0 for a complete valid stream, 1 for decode/truncation/read failures (prior valid events may already be printed), and 2 for decoder allocation failure. Use only gcc, make, and the standard C library. Run make test.
